C0.quote: a jury that has to select the deserving winner from a group of candidates
C0.note: Mechanism design/implementation paper: jurors' announcements are aggregated into a collective choice by a sequential voting-like mechanism; strategic aspects (backward induction) analysed. Borderline but treated as eligible.

C1.quote: implements the socially optimal rule via backward induction
C1.note: Implementation results: necessary condition (minimal impartiality) and a mechanism whose backward induction equilibrium yields the deserving winner. Some results are impossibility/characterisation-like, but most concern equilibrium outcomes.

C2.1.quote: Mi is a message space for agent i

C2.2.note: Input is an announcement of a single candidate (a message), not a ranking or approval set.

C2.3.quote: Each agent i has a preference function Ri
C2.3.note: Jurors have preferences over candidates depending on the deserving winner.

C2.4.note: Messages (announcements) and preference functions Ri are separate objects with separate notation; jurors may announce non-sincerely.

C3.1.quote: incentives to deceive emerge to prevent their enemy from being selected
C3.1.note: All analyses are of strategic jurors under backward induction.

C4.1.note: Input is not ranking/approval/etc.; no utility-type notions for voters beyond ordinal preferences.

C5.1.quote: The socially optimal outcome is the victory of this deserving winner.
C5.1.note: The socially optimal rule is a given deserving winner, not evaluated via welfare, efficiency, representation or distortion; it is the implementation target.

VOT.quote_behav: incentives to deceive to ensure that their favorite candidate is chosen
VOT.quote_info: known to all agents but cannot be verified
VOT.note: Jurors know the deserving winner (and, per sequential perfect information, others' moves); preferences beyond conflicts of interest partly unknown to planner. Jury configuration is common knowledge in comparison with Holzman-Moulin.

CAN.note: Candidates are identified with jurors; their only actions are as jurors, coded under VOT.

ORG.note: Planner designs the mechanism but is not an acting agent; no organiser actions in the model.

DES.note: Designer's objective is implementing the socially optimal rule, but no explicit modelling of designer choices as an agent; treated as the analyst's goal.

C8.1.quote: implements the socially optimal rule via backward induction
C8.1.note: Backward induction in finite perfect-information sequential mechanisms; also mentions Nash and dominant strategies only in discussion.

C8.2.quote: implements the socially optimal rule via backward induction

claims.quote: design a mechanism (or voting system) that incentivizes jurors to choose the deserving winner
we propose a novel, simple, and natural mechanism that successfully implements
it is reasonable to think that each juror will strive to favor

C9.1.note: Claims about applicability to international competitions and about which mechanism to use (natural mechanism that works).

C9.2.quote: each agent prioritizes their own victory, regardless of the deserving winner
C9.2.note: The claims follow from the formal model whose assumptions (preferences, common knowledge of deserving winner, strategic jurors, backward induction) are stated.
